Headline

The dominant arc of the past 96 hours is the conditional resolution of the US-Iran war and the downstream political fragility of that resolution. On June 14, President Trump declared the Iran deal "complete"dominicanrepublicpost.com with Strait of Hormuz reopening and full blockade removal, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif confirmed permanent termination of hostilitiesliveuamap.com. The next day, Oman-track talks were reported suspended, dimming the June 19 Geneva signing outlook. Three structural signals compete for attention: the Pentagon added 188 Chinese companies including BYD, Alibaba, and Baidu to its military-company contracting ban (Straits Timesstraitstimes.com); the SpaceX IPO raised $75 billion at a $2T+ valuation on June 12 (CNBCcnbc.com); and a US Army AH-64 Apache went down near the Strait of Hormuznbcdfw.com on June 9, a signal of how thin the operational margin was during the active phase. Watch areas Israel-Iran-Hezbollah axis and Russia oil sanctions perimeter both fired this cycle.

Central bank divergence + dollar funding (6 items): The 10y-2y spread at +41bp signals a curve that has un-inverted but has not yet achieved a steepness historically consistent with strong credit expansion. The 30-year at 5.01% creates fiscal drag on a $36T federal debt load.

Quiet today: Critical minerals, EM debt distress, AI compute/semiconductor export controls, Sahel jihadist corridor, Arctic/High North, Korean peninsula, Latin America.

Macro Situation

The US Treasury curve as of June 5 shows a positive but shallow 10y-2y spread of +41 basis pointsfred.stlouisfed.org. The 2-year sits at 4.17%fred.stlouisfed.org, the 10-year at 4.55%fred.stlouisfed.org, and the 30-year at 5.01%fred.stlouisfed.org. The 30-year printing above 5% is notable: since World War II, sustained 30-year yields above 5% have historically correlated with either elevated inflation expectations or a term-premium re-rating from fiscal uncertainty. The current reading likely reflects both. A $4T additional deficit from OBBBA over ten years, layered onto existing debt-to-GDP dynamics, creates a structural reason for long-end rates to stay elevated even as the Fed eases [high].

Easing

Fed Funds effective at 3.62%fred.stlouisfed.org and SOFR at 3.63%fred.stlouisfed.org confirm the Fed remains on hold after its May 2026 pause. Jerome Powell's tenure ended in May 2026conversableeconomist.com, according to the Conversable Economist's early retrospective. His successor faces a policy environment in which the curve has barely steepened off a prolonged inversion: in the 2019 analogue, the curve was at this slope level during preemptive easing, not neutral hold. The question of whether the next chair tilts dovish early, given the tariff-driven inflation overhang, is the primary macro variable for H2 2026 [medium].

United States Politics & Policy

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act remains the central fiscal event. Yale Budget Lab's combined distributional analysisbudgetlab.yale.edu finds that OBBBA tax cuts plus the 2025 tariff schedule reduce after-tax incomes for the bottom 10% by more than 6.5%, while lifting the top quintile by roughly 1.5%. The Senate floor schedule through June 20 is the critical path; the debt-ceiling component creates a procedural constraint that has forced Republican leadership to negotiate internal offsets.

Federal Register (June 9) produced 17 new items. The DEA MAT rulefederalregister.gov extends telehealth flexibilities for medication-assisted opioid treatment, a public-health continuity action. The NCUA preemption rulefederalregister.gov finalizes federal credit union fee preemption over state consumer protection law, a significant institutional win for the credit union lobby with downstream consumer consequences. The Copyright Office DMCA triennial proceeding (Round 10)federalregister.gov will determine AI training data access rules for 2027-2029; this is the most consequential copyright proceeding for generative AI companies since the first LLM wave. The CFTC's rescission of its settlements policyfederalregister.gov removes a constraint on respondents' ability to settle without admissions, a signal of regulatory deregulation in financial enforcement.

Campaign finance as of June 9: Jon Ossoff (Senate GA, Dem) leads all cycle 2026 fundraisers at $81.15M raisedfec.gov. James Talarico (Senate TX, Dem) at $40.28Mfec.gov and Cory Booker (Senate NJ, Dem) at $32.26Mfec.gov follow. Speaker Mike Johnson (House LA, Rep) at $17.55Mfec.gov is the senior Republican with cycle fundraising approaching competitive Democrats. Lindsey Graham (Senate SC, Rep) is in deficit position: $29.18M spentfec.gov against $20.92M raised, a $8.26M negative cash position that creates vulnerability heading into a contested cycle.

The federal judge ruling striking down the $100,000 H-1B visa feewkms.org is the most significant immigration-law ruling of the past week. The fee was designed to deter employer-sponsored skilled immigration by pricing out all but the largest corporations. The ruling, citing lack of statutory authority, will almost certainly be appealed, but it restores the prior H-1B regime pending higher-court review.

Russia & Post-Soviet

The EU 21st sanctions package is the week's Russia policy story. The Gazprom/Rosneft shadow fleet exposure to new maritime enforcement will be the test of whether this package has teeth beyond its predecessors. The ruble at 73.1 per dollar (from June 15 brief data) represents a multi-year strengthening from the 80-90 range, partly driven by Iran deal energy-market relief. A stronger ruble makes Russian consumer imports cheaper, which reduces inflation pressure on Putin's domestic approval but also reduces the energy-revenue-per-dollar Russia receives [medium]. Explosions were reported in Cheboksary (Russia) on June 13 per Liveuamap, consistent with ongoing Ukrainian long-range strike capability against rear-area targets.

The Iran deal's terms, insofar as they involve any Russian leverage as a secondary actor, have implications for Moscow's geopolitical positioning. Russia had indirect stakes in the Iran nuclear standoff as a Security Council member and as a shadow sanctions-busting partner for Tehran. A US-Iran normalization would reduce one of Russia's few remaining geopolitical levers outside the Ukraine theater [medium].

Ukraine Theater (Dedicated)

The frontline snapshot as of June 15 is based on the DeepStateMap daily cartographydeepstatemap.live, covering 522 polygons. Frontline resolution is approximately 1 kilometer; this brief does NOT claim meter-level Russian unit positions, which open-source data does not support.

Anomaly

The most significant operational signal in the June 14-15 FIRMS data is the thermal anomaly cluster in the Kherson and Mykolaiv oblasts: 101 hotspots with a total fire radiative power of 787.7 MW. This is the dominant thermal cluster by an order of magnitude versus any other zone in the theater. The Zaporizhzhia oblast cluster (10 hotspots, 122.5 MW total FRP) and the Sumy oblast cluster (29 hotspots, 69.2 MW) are secondary. The Dnipropetrovsk oblast (22 hotspots, 66.6 MW) and Chernihiv oblast (15 hotspots, 43.6 MW) round out the active zones. FIRMS resolution is 375 meters for VIIRS; thermal anomalies at this resolution reflect large fires, munitions impacts, or industrial events but cannot distinguish between them.

The highest individual FIRMS reading (9.92 MW) at latitude 48.533, longitude 34.645 falls in the Dnipropetrovsk oblast, near the Kryvyi Rih industrial zone. The Kherson/Mykolaiv cluster's dominance (787.7 MW vs. 122.5 MW for the next-highest zone) is consistent with ongoing shelling activity along the Dnipro River left-bank line, where Russia and Ukraine have maintained contested positions.

Operationally, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reportedliveuamap.com clashes on June 15 at the Orikhiv direction, near Stepove, Stepnohirsk, and towards Prymorske. This front (northwestern Zaporizhzhia oblast) has been a consistent pressure point. Separately, smoke was reported rising in Starobilskliveuamap.com (Luhansk oblast) after morning shelling on June 13, consistent with Ukrainian long-range fires reaching rear-area logistics nodes.

Cyber & Biosecurity

FIRST-OF-KIND KEV CALLOUT: CVE-2026-42271nvd.nist.gov is a command injection vulnerability in BerriAI LiteLLM, an LLM application framework used as a proxy layer for routing calls to multiple AI models. This is the first vulnerability in an LLM application framework to be added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. What makes this structurally significant: the KEV catalog has now entered the agentic AI software stack. Prior KEV additions targeted operating systems, network devices, enterprise databases, and productivity software. LiteLLM is an orchestration layer sitting between applications and LLM APIs; its compromise provides an attacker with API key access, model output manipulation capability, and potential lateral movement into backend systems. Remediation deadline: June 22, 2026.

CVE-2026-50751nvd.nist.gov affects Check Point Security Gateway with an improper authentication flaw; remediation deadline June 11 (past). Check Point Security Gateway sits on the perimeter of enterprise and government networks globally; exploitation of an authentication bypass at the perimeter is a high-priority remediation. The prior KEV additions in the June window include CVE-2026-28318 (SolarWinds Serv-U)nvd.nist.gov, CVE-2026-48027 (Nx Console, ransomware-linked)nvd.nist.gov, and CVE-2026-45321 (TanStack, ransomware-linked)nvd.nist.gov. The Nx Console and TanStack entries reflect a ransomware escalation into JavaScript developer toolchain packages, a category not previously prominent in KEV.

The Conversable Economist's retrospective on Jerome Powellconversableeconomist.com (June 8) is the most analytically important commentary piece this cycle. Powell's eight-year tenure navigated the largest inflation surge since the 1970s and the fastest rate-hiking cycle since Volcker. The piece implicitly raises the question of whether his successor will have the institutional independence to hold rates elevated if the political pressure to ease accelerates under OBBBA's deficit implications. Historical Context

The GDELT tone heatmap over the past four weeks shows the Middle East region at a sustained average tone of -6.5 to -7.2, the most negative on the global screen. This is consistent with the Iran war operational phase from late February through mid-June. By comparison, Russia/FSU tone has been consistently negative at -4.2 to -5.1, reflecting the combination of Ukraine-war coverage and the EU sanctions packages.

The historical analogue most relevant to the current Iran deal trajectory is the Libya 2003 model: Gaddafi's WMD renunciation produced a rapid normalization that lasted until 2011, when a different set of grievances collapsed the arrangement. If the US-Iran deal is structurally robust (involving Iranian nuclear transparency and Hormuz non-blockade commitments), the 20-year precedent suggests it can hold through one or two administrations before external shocks test it. If it is primarily a ceasefire of convenience, the 6-12 month window before internal Iranian politics reasserts itself is the historical danger zone [medium].

The SpaceX IPO at $2T+ on day one places it in the same historical category as Saudi Aramco (largest IPO by dollar amount, 2019) and China Agricultural Bank (2010). Each of those events had a macro-credit signal attached: Aramco's $29.4B IPO preceded Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 diversification push; the Chinese bank IPOs were instruments of state recapitalization. SpaceX is neither of these things, but a private US tech company reaching $2T on day one of listing represents a new structural reality for venture-capital terminal-value pricing [medium].
